unchecked_sentences.text: The unit is a hinge that is on when x has no open piece on that diagonal and off once x has one: on the 49405 training rows with the count at zero it is on for a share 1.00 of them, and on the 4640 rows where x has an open piece on d6-g3 it is on for 0 of them.

Its weight on the input is -1.47 per sd and its edge into the output logit is 0.043, so the effect is tiny: in the typical position the predicted chance of an x win is 49% with the count at zero and 49% with one x piece on the line (whole model; the unit goes from 0.46 to 0.00).
Switching the part off changes the mean predicted chance by 0.002 and the training AUC from 0.912 to 0.912.
Game reading: x having an open piece on the high diagonal d6-g3 on the right side of the board removes a small bonus; the library concept x_line_d6-g3 predicts the unit with score 1.00.
Closed form from get_formula over z-scored inputs (per sd), coefficients rounded to three significant figures; it reproduces the exit on the training rows to a maximum absolute error of 1.0e-03.

The unit is a hinge with a rule that holds on the training rows: it is on when x's open count on b5-e2 is at least o's open count on b3-b6 and off otherwise (0 of the 50930 rows with x's count at least o's have it off; 0 of the 3115 rows with o's count larger have it on).
Most off rows are o stacking column b with x absent from the crossing diagonal: 3040 rows have o on open b3-b6 and no x on b5-e2, with an observed x-win rate of 0.56 against 0.66 for the rest.
When on, the unit rises with x's pieces on b5-e2 (weight 0.24 per sd) and falls with o's pieces on b3-b6 (-0.22 per sd), and feeds the output logit with weight 0.88.

Self-probe (whole model, typical position): with no o on b3-b6, x pieces on b5-e2 at zero, one, two and three give predicted x-win chances of 49%, 61%, 72% and 81%; with no x on b5-e2, one o piece on b3-b6 switches the unit off and drops the chance from 49% to 35%, and more o pieces change nothing f
Switching the part off lowers the mean predicted chance by 0.072 and the training AUC from 0.912 to 0.910: it is the largest nonlinear part but a small part of the whole.

Game reading: the model treats o building an open stack up column b, unanswered by x on the diagonal through b5, as bad for x; the concept 'x count on b5-e2 at least o count on b3-b6' predicts the gate with score 1.00.
Closed form from get_formula over z-scored inputs (per sd), coefficients rounded to three significant figures; it reproduces the exit on the training rows to a maximum absolute error of 1.4e-03.

On the training rows the ReLU is on for every row (a share 1.00 of the 54045 rows), so this part is a straight line in x_thr_even: weight 0.67 per sd into the unit and -0.098 from the unit into the output logit, so through this part more x even-row threats lower x's predicted chance.

The same input's direct edge, in the aggregates part, is 0.093 per sd, so in the whole model an x even-row threat still raises the predicted chance: in the typical position zero, one and two such threats give 49%, 55% and 61%.
The input is rare: 594 training rows have at least one x even-row threat (observed x-win rate 0.83) and 54 have two or more.
The library concept x_thr_even predicts the unit with score 1.00; the part is a linear rescaling of its input that partly cancels its own direct term, so it is described, not explained in game terms.
